h1:
Nonthaburi on a Budget
Metro + Ferry, a Full Day Under 1,000 THB
intro: Nonthaburi might be the best-value escape near Bangkok. The MRT Purple Line drops you into town for a flat 20 THB, then a ferry to Koh Kret costs just 3–5 THB, and the riverside food is still priced for locals, not tourists. We've laid out the plan as day-by-day blocks — real transport costs, real food, and a running total per person. Read to the end and you can leave today.

blocks.html: If you assume a trip near Bangkok has to be expensive, Nonthaburi will change your mind. Almost everything here is built around public transport. The MRT Purple Line runs from Tao Poon to Khlong Bang Phai, passing the Nonthaburi Civic Center, the Ministry of Public Health, and out toward Bang Yai — and from there you can cross the Chao Phraya River to Koh Kret for spare change. We walked it and checked the real prices: fares, ferries, and food, so you can plan with hard numbers instead of guessing.

blocks.text: The real per-person cost of one day in Nonthaburi

blocks.html: Let's start with the numbers, because this is exactly why people pick Nonthaburi for a cheap day off. Here's roughly what one person spends in a day, coming in from central Bangkok by metro.

items: MRT Purple Line — flat 20 THB per ride, so 40 THB round trip (you have to register for the fare cap in the Thang Rat app first, otherwise it's the distance-based 14–42 THB)
Ferry to Koh Kret — 6–10 THB round trip, depending on the pier and the day
Lunch + riverside snacks — 100–200 THB if you stick to local stalls
Temple and site entry — mostly free; donate as you wish
Full-day total — about 250–450 THB per person, not even half a thousand

blocks.title: Register first for the cheapest fare
blocks.html: The flat 20 THB cap on the Purple Line is a benefit you have to register for: link your national ID in the Thang Rat app and connect a Rabbit card, an EMV card, or MRT Plus ahead of time. Tap a plain card and you'll pay the standard 14–42 THB. Sort it out at home before you head out.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Nonthaburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.text: How to chain the metro and ferry for the best value

blocks.html: The whole budget plan hinges on smooth transfers. The Purple Line connects to other lines at several points, so you can reach Nonthaburi from almost any corner of Bangkok without touching a car.

items: Coming from the city center — take the Blue Line (MRT) to Tao Poon and walk across the platform straight onto the Purple Line; you never leave the system
Coming from the east — the Pink Line meets the Purple Line at Nonthaburi Civic Center station (Sun Khae Rai); get off and transfer right there

Getting to Koh Kret — take the cross-river ferry from Wat Sanam Nuea pier to Wat Pramai Yikawat pier, 3 THB during the day (5 THB early morning and evening); the Wat Klang Kret–Pa Fai pier route costs the same
Cruise the river — from Tha Nam Non you can board a Chao Phraya Express boat for a low double-digit fare if you want the full riverside view

blocks.title: Weekdays are cheaper and quieter
blocks.html: Some piers charge 5 THB on weekends but 3 THB on weekdays. The difference is small, but the real bonus is that Koh Kret is far less crowded on a weekday — much easier to wander, take photos, and graze on snacks.

blocks.text: Day-by-day blocks — pick by how much time you have

blocks.html: We've laid out two options. Day one is a full day on Koh Kret and the riverside; day two is a temple–market–café crawl along the metro line. If you only have one day, do day one. If you're staying over or coming back for a second round, run them back to back.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Koh Kret + the riverside, cheap eats all day

items.activity: Ride the Purple Line to the station nearest the ferry, then catch a ride to Wat Sanam Nuea pier
items.note: Head out a bit early to dodge the midday heat while walking the island

items.activity: Take the cross-river ferry to Koh Kret, 3 THB per person
items.note: Ferries run often, so no long wait; you land at Wat Pramai Yikawat pier

items.activity: Pay respects at the Mon-style pagoda at Wat Pramai Yikawat, then walk into the community market
items.note: The temple is free to enter and is the heart of the island's Mon culture

items.activity: Graze on the island's signature bites — tod man no kala (fried fish cake with local bamboo shoot), khanom tuay fu (steamed flower cups), and Mon-style khao chae
items.note: Fried fish cakes run a few tens of baht a plate, a khao chae set around 60 THB — you can eat your fill for under 200 THB

items.activity: Stop at a Thai sweets shop for small souvenirs, 3–12 THB a piece
items.note: Pick the ones with auspicious names — cheap, cute gifts to bring home

items.activity: Browse the Mon pottery, made by the island's old earthenware community
items.note: Photograph it all day; there's no entry fee

items.activity: Sit at a riverside spot with a coffee or iced tea and watch the boats go by on the Chao Phraya
items.note: Drinks run 40–70 THB a glass — a good rest before you cross back

items.activity: Ferry back to the Nonthaburi side and ride the Purple Line home
items.note: The return ferry is another 3 THB; your whole day's transport is just a few tens of baht

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Temples, markets, and cafés along the metro line

items.activity: Get off the Purple Line near the Ministry of Public Health and stroll the leafy government district
items.note: Several spots have coffee at student-and-civil-servant prices, cheaper than the malls

items.activity: Visit Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat Worawihan by the river, with architecture from the reign of King Rama III
items.note: Free to enter, quiet and calm, and great for photos

items.activity: Have lunch around Tha Nam Non, the city's big community market
items.note: Noodles, rice-and-curry, made-to-order dishes — 40–70 THB a plate, with plenty to choose from

items.activity: Walk the Tha Nam Non market for fruit, dried goods, and sweets
items.note: Nonthaburi is famous for its durian — if you come in season, hunt some down to taste

items.activity: Rest your legs at a riverside café or Somdet Phra Sri Nakharin Park
items.note: The park is free — a green lung in the middle of town, nice for a walk and photos

items.activity: Hop back on the Purple Line and close out the trip with your wallet intact
items.note: Today's spending is mostly food and coffee; the fare is still just 20 THB flat

blocks.html: The value of Nonthaburi lives in its food, because it's still priced for the community, not for tourists. Here's what to track down, ranked by how worth-trying and how wallet-friendly it is.

items.name: Tod man no kala (bamboo-shoot fish cakes)
items.blurb: Koh Kret's signature dish — fried fish cakes made with no kala, a local bamboo shoot. Firm, fragrant, and eaten with cucumber relish. If you come to the island, you order this.

items.name: Mon-style khao chae
items.blurb: Rice in chilled, flower-scented water, eaten with an array of sides — fried shrimp-paste balls, sweet shredded pork, stuffed sweet peppers. An old-fashioned way to beat the heat.

items.name: Auspicious-name Thai sweets
items.blurb: Thong yip, thong yod, met khanun, ja mongkut — made fresh in the Koh Kret community and cheap, pretty gifts to take home.

items.name: Boat noodles & made-to-order at Tha Nam Non
items.blurb: The Tha Nam Non market has rice-and-curry shops, made-to-order stalls, and noodle vendors lined up in a row at true community prices — a full meal for a few tens of baht.

items.name: Khanom tuay fu (flower steamed cups)
items.blurb: Colorful steamed rice cups shaped like flowers, handmade by the community and hard to find in Bangkok. Very cheap and easy to snack on while you walk.

items.name: Nonthaburi durian (seasonal)
items.blurb: If you come in durian season, Nonthaburi is a famous source. It costs more than usual because the real thing is rare — but tasting it once is worth the experience.

items: Bring a water bottle — walking Koh Kret under the midday sun, buying bottle after bottle adds up fast; carrying your own helps a lot
Eat your main meal at Tha Nam Non, snack on Koh Kret — spend smart: fill up at the community market and save room for the island's standout bites
Skip the stalls right at the main entrance — the shops deeper inside the community are usually cheaper and genuinely better
Check the last ferry time — the cross-river ferry stops running in the evening; don't get so caught up that you miss it
Buy souvenirs on the island, not at the entrance — Thai sweets and pottery inside the community are priced better than at the tourist spots

faq.q: How much does one day in Nonthaburi cost?
faq.a: If you travel by the MRT Purple Line and the cross-river ferry and eat local at the markets and on Koh Kret, the total runs about 250–450 THB per person per day. Actual transport is only a few tens of baht, since the metro is a flat 20 THB and the ferry is just 3–5 THB.

faq.q: Where do you catch the ferry to Koh Kret, and how much is it?
faq.a: The popular crossings are Wat Sanam Nuea to Wat Pramai Yikawat, or Wat Klang Kret to Pa Fai. The ferry is 3 THB per person during the day and 5 THB early morning and evening; some piers charge 5 THB on weekends.

faq.q: What do you need to do first for the flat 20 THB Purple Line fare?
faq.a: Register the benefit with your national ID in the Thang Rat app, then link it to a Rabbit card, an EMV credit/debit card, or MRT Plus. Without registering, you'll pay the standard distance-based 14–42 THB.

faq.q: Is it better to visit Nonthaburi on a weekday or a weekend?
faq.a: Weekdays are far less crowded, so it's easier to walk Koh Kret and take photos, and some ferries are cheaper too. But if you want a lively market with every shop open, weekends have more buzz.

faq.q: What are the cheap eats you shouldn't miss in Nonthaburi?
faq.a: Bamboo-shoot fish cakes and Mon-style khao chae on Koh Kret, auspicious-name Thai sweets that cost just a few baht each to take home, and made-to-order dishes and noodles at community prices at the Tha Nam Non market.
